svg.text: #20 — MSG_SPLICE_PAGES hands TCP a page that nothing holds a reference to
The sender completes the bio, and its pages are recycled, while the data is still queued for the NIC. Fixed twice: 4f1f6b1c63e8 (copy, to prove the model), 0908ab370b05 (MSG_ZEROCOPY).
1 · pcache_send_bio_pages() — hand the bio's own pages to TCP
iov_iter_bvec(&iter, ITER_SOURCE, bvec, nr, len);
sock_sendmsg(sock, &msg); /* msg_flags |= MSG_SPLICE_PAGES */
The comment above this code read: "Mirrors DRBD's _drbd_send_page() pattern".
2 · the splice path takes NO page reference
skb_splice_from_iter() → iov_iter_extract_pages()
→ iov_iter_extract_bvec_pages():
(*pages)[k++] = bv.bv_page; /* no get_page() */
The skb frag now points at a bio page that nothing pinned.
3 · sock_sendmsg() returns — the data is not on the wire
It is still in the TCP send queue / qdisc / NIC tx ring. The page must stay
valid until the LAST skb referencing it is released — and under this flag
the sender is never told when that happens.
Rule the sender assumed: sendmsg() returned ⇒ the page is mine again. ✗
Meanwhile — four paths complete the bio early
Every one of them was added for a correct reason:
1) pcache_req_put(preq, 0) right after the send returns (6adc8d2a8d08)
2) ACK timeout reclaim — 30 s, so that a bio never hangs
3) pcache_flush_stream() on link down — completes all pending
4) pcache_net_stop() / pcache_flush_pending() teardown
3) can fire milliseconds after sendmsg() returned. That is the worst one.
All four are failure paths — which is why steady state never shows this:
F41 alone, 10 rounds, completely clean; F41/F42 under churn, always hit.
whichever fires first,
it lands here
4 · bio_endio() — the page is freed and reused while the NIC has not read it yet
The last reference to the request goes away → bio_endio() → the page returns to whoever allocated it, and is then written by someone else.
The NIC DMAs whatever the page holds at that moment. What reaches the peer is not what the write contained — frame header included.
5 · what it looks like on the peer — full regression run, netconsole capture
44513.188576 enp1s0: bad gso: type: 1b, size: 0, flags 24 tunnel 0
44513.198732 dm-pcache: secondary: unknown packet type (+10 ms)
44550.689146 VM_BUG_ON_PAGE(page_ref_count(page) == 0) → panic (+37.5 s)
virtio_net rejects the frame: its GSO header is illegal — exactly what a rewritten page produces
the byte stream is now desynced; 15100 such errors followed
NOT this defect — the receiver never sends bio pages. See #23.
The copy fix drove bad gso 1 → 0 and stream corruption 15100 → 2, and the run went 166/4 → 180 PASS / 0 FAIL.
Why the same mechanism is safe in DRBD: the premise, not the code
/* We may not do this for protocol A, where we could
* complete a write before the network stack sends the data. */
msg_flags = proto_b_or_c && !digest_size ? MSG_SPLICE_PAGES : 0;
DRBD splices only where the protocol forbids completing a write before
the data is out. Protocol A always copies. Plus per-page sendpage_ok(),
a drbd_disable_sendpage switch, and a copy whenever a digest is on.
pcache-dist is Protocol C — on paper it qualifies. The four paths above
break the premise, so the mechanism was never safe here.
Fix — MSG_ZEROCOPY (0908ab370b05): the path that does pin the page
zerocopy_fill_skb_from_iter() → iov_iter_get_pages2()
bvec branch: folio_get() ← the reference splice never took
msg.msg_ubuf = &uarg; msg.msg_flags |= MSG_ZEROCOPY;
uarg.flags = SKBFL_ZEROCOPY_FRAG | SKBFL_DONT_ORPHAN;
The stack calls uarg->ops->complete() when the last skb holding the page
is released, so the sender is finally told. Leave those flags at 0 and
skb_zcopy() never sees the skb: complete() never runs, first write hangs.
2641 MiB/s vs 2646 for the unsafe splice, vs 1959 copying — cost recovered.
Reading: borrowing a mechanism from DRBD without its guard condition is more dangerous than an explicit divergence — it looks consistent.
Scope: the bad gso signal is this defect. The page BUG that first pointed here is not — four builds, with and without splice, died alike (#23).
